Assessment
45-year-old male (MRN SYN-6122281) presenting with an 11-week history of an intensely pruritic rash on the flexor wrists, forearms, and shins refractory to 7 weeks of topical clotrimazole 1% cream, accompanied by 2 months of burning oral mucosal discomfort and mild transaminase elevation.

1. Primary Diagnosis: Cutaneous and Oral Erosive Lichen Planus (with hypertrophic shin plaques and desquamative gingivitis).
- Basis for diagnosis: Physical exam demonstrates classic "6 Ps" of cutaneous lichen planus—pruritic, purple (violaceous), polygonal, planar (flat-topped), shiny papules and plaques on the flexor wrists and forearms with overlying fine white lacy lines (Wickham striae), a linear streak of identical papules along a healed forearm scratch (Koebner phenomenon), and thicker hyperkeratotic/hypertrophic plaques on the shins. Dental exam (2024-05-15) confirms bilateral buccal mucosal lacy white reticular striae with shallow painful erosions (non-wipeable, no adjacent amalgam fillings) and lower desquamative gingivitis.
